page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.48xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture using AWS Neoverse-V2 cores. The configuration features 192 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock of 2.7 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding symmetric multithreading contention. Per-core cache allocations include 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, supported by a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 400 Gbps, has no bundled local storage, and includes zero graphics processing units.

Benchmark results show strong parallel execution metrics driven by the 192 dedicated physical cores. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU performance reaches 311,843.21, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, while single-core performance settles in the middle 50 percent at 1,643.9. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, recording 960.61 GB/sec on uncached read-only large blocks and 483.46 GB/sec on write operations. Highly parallelized workloads scale effectively, evidenced by a Geekbench clang software compilation score of 85,768.0, 359.39 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, and 230.42 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, workloads reliant on vector acceleration or single-threaded execution exhibit average results, and small-model LLM prompt processing places in the lower 25 percent.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance maximizes resource density per host by offering 192 full physical cores alongside massive network throughput. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires remote storage attachments, which represents an architectural consideration for I/O-intensive pipelines. The balanced memory ratio and top-tier multi-threaded compute render m8gb.48xlarge well configured for large-scale distributed databases, high-concurrency web serving fleets, enterprise CI/CD compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing frameworks.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.48xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual server powered by 192 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz with 768.0 GB of memory and 400 Gbps baseline networking. Without local SSD storage or GPU acceleration, this configuration relies on network-attached storage while emphasizing core density and high memory throughput, recording 960.61 GB/sec in uncached memory reads and over 359 million Redis SET operations per second. Multi-threaded compute benchmarks place in the top tier, contrasting with moderate single-core ratings. The server is suited for high-concurrency web applications, parallel CI/CD code builds, and distributed database workloads.
